## Simple explanation

Fine-tuning takes a model that has already been trained and continues
training it on examples related to a particular task or domain.

## Technical explanation

Fine-tuning initializes from pretrained parameters and optimizes some or
all of them using task-specific data and an objective. Methods include
full fine-tuning and parameter-efficient approaches such as adapters or
low-rank updates. Data quality, learning rate, and training duration
affect retention and adaptation.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Fine-tuning can adapt a model's style, task behaviour, or domain
performance. It requires suitable data, careful evaluation, and ongoing
model-version management; it is not always the best solution for
knowledge that changes frequently.

## How it works

Prepare training and evaluation datasets, initialize the model from a
pretrained checkpoint, and continue optimization under an appropriate
objective. Evaluate the fine-tuned model on target tasks and regression
tests to identify improvements and capability losses.

## Practical example

A pretrained text classifier can be fine-tuned on labeled support
messages to route them into a team's categories, then evaluated on
held-out conversations from the intended deployment setting.

## Common misconceptions

- Fine-tuning is not the same as prompting or retrieval-augmented
  generation.
- More fine-tuning data or epochs do not automatically improve results.
- Fine-tuning can cause regressions or overfit if evaluation is
  inadequate.
